title: Polynomial-presentation comparisons for the sheaf naive cotangent complex
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a sheaf of sets $E$ with map $\alpha:E\to B$, let $P_E=A[E]$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $U\mapsto A(U)[E(U)]$, with restriction of coefficients and variables; polynomial rings use [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Suppose evaluation $P_E\to B$, $[e]\mapsto\alpha(e)$, is surjective as a sheaf map. Put $J_E=\ker(P_E\to B)$, an ideal subsheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-ideal], and let $J_E^2$ consist locally of finite sums of products of sections of $J_E$. Write $M_E=J_E/J_E^2$, $F_E=\Omega_{P_E/A}\otimes_{P_E}B$ and $K_E=[M_E\xrightarrow{d_E}F_E]$ in degrees $-1,0$, where $d_E(\bar j)=\mathrm dj\otimes1$. Here differentials are the sheafification of the sectionwise universal modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and tensor products are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Define $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}=K_B$ using $E=B$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$, and write $\Omega_{B/A}$ for the sheafified sectionwise differential module. There are canonical isomorphisms $\lambda_E:K_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$. If $v:E\to E'$ is a map over $B$ between such presentations, the induced chain map $K(v):K_E\to K_{E'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\lambda_{E'}K(v)=\lambda_E$. These comparisons are compatible with identity maps and composition. The canonical map $F_E\to\Omega_{B/A}$ induces $\operatorname{coker}(d_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{B/A}$.

source.place: Tag 08TY (lemma-NL-up-to-qis), including naturality of the canonical comparison under maps of sheaf generators; Tag 08TS (lemma-differential-seq), for the cokernel identification.

proof.text: Put $Q(U)=A(U)[E(U)]$, $C(U)=\operatorname{im}(Q(U)\to B(U))$ and $I(U)=\ker(Q(U)\to B(U))$. These are presheaves with the evident restriction maps; $Q\to C$ is sectionwise surjective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-image-presheaf-sheafification-iso] to $Q\to B$: its sheafification is the assumed surjection $P_E\to B$, so $C\subset B$ is locally surjective and $C^\#=B$. All objects and values lie in the chosen universe. We will use the ring presentation $Q(U)\twoheadrightarrow C(U)$, never assume $Q(U)\to B(U)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 08TY (lemma-NL-up-to-qis), proof of the claim: definition of the image presheaf B′.

proof.text: Sheafify the sectionwise two-term complex $T_E(U)=[I(U)/I(U)^2\to\Omega_{Q(U)/A(U)}\otimes_{Q(U)}C(U)]$. Its terms have their extended sheaf-module structures by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. Exactness of abelian sheafification ([lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], with the fixed ring $\mathbf Z$) gives $I^\#=J_E$. By the local representation and local equality clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], $(I^2)^\#=J_E^2$: a finite sum of products of local sections of $J_E$ locally lifts to the same finite sum of products of sections of $I$, and conversely each such sum lands in $J_E^2$. Exactness then gives $(I/I^2)^\#=J_E/J_E^2$. The differential term becomes $F_E$: [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel] identifies the sheafified differential module with $\Omega_{P_E/A}$, while [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor], applied over the presheaf of rings $Q$ to the presheaves of $Q$-modules $\Omega_{Q/A}$ and $C$ (with $Q^\#=P_E$, $C^\#=B$), gives $(\Omega_{Q/A}\otimes_{p,Q}C)^\#\cong\Omega_{P_E/A}\otimes_{P_E}B$ in the sense of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Explicitly this map sends $\mathrm dq\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d\eta_Q(q)\otimes\eta_C(c)$. These identifications carry $\bar i\mapsto\mathrm di\otimes1$ to $d_E$. Thus $T_E^\#$ is $K_E$ as a complex. Exact sheafification also commutes with its kernels and cokernels. The same formulas show compatibility with every generator map over $B$.

source.place: Tag 08TY, proof of the claim (sheafification of the kernel complex), using Tag 08TP (lemma-differentials-sheafify).

proof.text: For each $U$, compare the polynomial presentation $Q(U)\twoheadrightarrow C(U)$ to the canonical one $A(U)[C(U)]\twoheadrightarrow C(U)$ by $[e]\mapsto[\alpha(e)]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentations-homotopy-equivalent] it induces an isomorphism on the kernels of the conormal differentials. These kernel identifications commute with restrictions and with maps of generators: [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] says that the kernel map is independent of the chosen lift and respects composition, including when base rings change. Applying step 2 gives $H^{-1}(K_E)=\mathcal T_C^\#$. Now apply [lem-sfb-locally-dense-cotangent-h1] to $C\subset B$, whose local-density hypothesis was proved in step 1. This gives a canonical isomorphism $H^{-1}(K_E)\cong\mathcal T_B^\#$. For $E=B$ the image presheaf is already $B$. The comparison for $E\to B$ induces precisely this isomorphism: its map to the canonical presentation of $B(U)$ factors through the canonical presentation of $C(U)$ by the displayed generator formula. Thus it is an isomorphism in degree $-1$.

source.place: Tag 08TY, proof of the claim, reduction to ring presentation independence and local-density invariance; Algebra Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy).

proof.text: The same ring presentation comparison identifies $H^0(T_E(U))$ with the cokernel for $A(U)[C(U)]\to C(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-naive-cotangent-complex-cokernel-kahler] this is $\Omega_{C(U)/A(U)}$. This identification is the evaluation map: $\mathrm dq\otimes c\mapsto c\,\mathrm d(\operatorname{ev}(q))$; it commutes with restriction and generator maps because these formulas agree on every $\mathrm dq$. Exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] and [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel], applied to $A\to C$ with $C^\#=B$, give $\operatorname{coker}(d_E)\cong\Omega_{B/A}$. The map is exactly the canonical $F_E\to\Omega_{B/A}$ in the statement. In particular $K_E\to K_B$ induces the identity of $\Omega_{B/A}$ in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 08TS (lemma-differential-seq), equivalently its proof by sectionwise cokernels and exact sheafification; Tag 08TY, H^0 paragraph.

proof.text: The polynomial map $P_E\to P_B$, $[e]\mapsto[\alpha(e)]$, sends $J_E$ and $J_E^2$ into $J_B$ and $J_B^2$. On the differential terms use $\mathrm dp\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm d f(p)\otimes b$. The universal differential property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] makes these maps linear, and on $\bar j$ the two chain-map composites both give $\mathrm d f(j)\otimes1$. Leibniz gives $\mathrm d(jj')\otimes1=0$ for $j,j'\in J_E$, so the conormal formula is well defined. Steps 3 and 4 show this chain map is a quasi-isomorphism, since both complexes vanish outside degrees $-1,0$. Define $\lambda_E$ to be its image in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; it is invertible by the definition of that localization. For $v:E\to E'$ over $B$, the equality $\alpha'v=\alpha$ gives $P(\alpha')P(v)=P(\alpha)$ by the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. On conormal classes and differential generators this yields the actual chain-map equality $K(\alpha')K(v)=K(\alpha)$, hence $\lambda_{E'}K(v)=\lambda_E$. On cohomology the two outer maps are isomorphisms, so $K(v)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Identity and composition follow by the same generator formulas.
